answer: Each identity binds one microchipped pet: a Willow Vet implants the chip, registers it in the Shale Registry, and the owner locks a 25 POA bond for 120 days. A chip costs 40 POA; a second under one name pays double, a third four times, capped at 320 POA, so 100 fakes cost about 33,800 POA, against 65 POA for one honest owner, each extra fake dearer than the last. The Tundra archive keeps 24 months of vet records, and yearly the vet re-scans the chip within 30 days; two missed scans forfeit half the bond and freeze payouts 3 epochs. Petless owners adopt via a shelter, with a doubled bond.
